title: Calisthenics Program
warmup: 2 min easy cardio — jog in place, jumping jacks, skipping
Wrists: palms down rocks ×10 · palms up rocks ×10 · fist circles ×10 — before any handstand work
10 bodyweight squats · 10 hip hinges · world's greatest stretch ×5/side
One light set of the first exercise, then a second at half your working load

reference.heading: Double progression
reference.body: Stay at the same variation until you hit the top of the rep range on every set, two sessions in a row. Then add load (backpack) if possible, otherwise move to the harder variation. When you progress, you drop back to the bottom of the range. That's normal. One deliberate exception: Phase 1 pull-ups, which have their own rule written on the exercise.

reference.heading: Supersets
reference.body: Exercises bracketed together alternate. Do one set of the first, wait the shown rest, one set of the second, wait, and repeat. Because the two movements don't compete, each one still gets roughly double the shown rest before its own next set — a 1:30 alternation gives every pull-up set about 3 minutes of recovery. This is what makes the session fit in 45 minutes without shortening anything that matters.

reference.heading: Effort
reference.body: Leave 1–2 reps in the tank on most sets. Going to failure every set on 4 days/week will bury your recovery. The last set of an exercise can go close to failure.

reference.heading: Rest between sets
reference.body: The timer shows the alternation interval, not your recovery. On the paired compound work each movement still gets 2–3 minutes before you repeat it. Don't cut it — short rests are the main reason people get tired quickly and then stall, because you end up limited by fatigue rather than strength, which is the wrong stimulus.

reference.heading: Order
reference.body: Skill work goes first, right after the warm-up, when you're fresh. Never at the end.

reference.heading: Adding the backpack
reference.body: Once you're loading a movement, don't go from the warm-up straight into a working set. Do one set at bodyweight and one at about half your working load first. It costs three minutes and it's the difference between elbows that tolerate weighted pull-ups and elbows that don't.

reference.heading: Advancing phases
reference.body: Never advance by calendar. Advance when you hit every criterion on the phase gate. The gates are the only clock in this program.

reference.heading: Retesting
reference.body: Retest when you think you're close to a gate, not on a schedule. Fresh day, full warm-up, one all-out set of pull-ups, one of dips, one max wall handstand hold. Do the retest instead of that session's first exercise, not on top of it.

reference.heading: Missed a session
reference.body: Take the sessions in order, not by weekday. If you miss Thursday, Upper B is simply what you do next. Never stack two sessions in a day to catch up, and never do the same session twice running to get back on the calendar — the order matters, the weekday doesn't. If you miss a whole week, repeat the last week's loads rather than picking up where the numbers left off.

reference.heading: Deload
reference.body: Every 6–8 weeks, or whenever your numbers go backwards three sessions running at the same load: one week at half the sets, same reps. Keep skill practice. Two bad sessions is noise — sleep, food, a cold bar. Three is a signal. Also deload if poor sleep, achy joints and flat motivation turn up together, whatever the numbers say.

reference.heading: Nutrition — the actual limiting factor
reference.body: At 66 kg, food is what's holding back muscle growth, not training. Eat ~300–400 kcal above maintenance, targeting 0.4–0.7 kg gained per month — about 0.25–0.5% of bodyweight per week. Slower than that and you're leaving most of the result on the table; faster and you're mostly adding fat. If the scale hasn't moved in three weeks, eat more. Protein 110–130 g/day across 3–4 meals. Sleep 7–9 hours.

reference.heading: Progressing a band
reference.body: Bands jump in big steps, so exhaust the small adjustments first: stand wider on the band, then choke up on it, then slow the lowering to 3 seconds. Move to a thicker band only when all three stop working.

reference.heading: Still getting tired quickly after 3 weeks?
reference.body: Breathing and heart rate spiking means conditioning — add two 20–30 min easy walks or rides on off days. Muscles burning out and arms giving up means you're resting too little between sets — time your rests for two weeks and see what changes.

skills.name: Muscle-up
skills.goal: One clean rep on the bar

phases.name: Phase 1
phases.span: Where you start. Leave when you clear the Phase 2 gate, however long that takes.

exercises.name: Wall handstand
exercises.note: Chest to wall. Stop before failure — this is practice, not a set.

exercises.name: Pull-ups
exercises.note: Exception to the progression rule: don't wait for all six sets. Add one rep to one set each week — 2,2,2,2,2,2 → 3,2,2,2,2,2 → 3,3,2,2,2,2. At 6×3, retest your max. Six clean doubles beats three ugly fives.

exercises.name: Dips
exercises.note: Full range, controlled.

exercises.name: Inverted rows
exercises.note: Park bar at hip height. Squeeze at the top.

exercises.name: Pike push-ups
exercises.note: Elevate the feet once this gets easy.

exercises.name: Band curls
exercises.note: Elbows pinned to your sides. 2 seconds down.

exercises.name: Band face pulls
exercises.note: Elbows high, hands finish beside your ears. Not a progression lift — keep it at 15 quality reps.

exercises.name: Tuck L-sit
exercises.note: On dip bars or the floor.

exercises.name: Bulgarian split squat
exercises.note: Load the backpack once you pass 12.

exercises.name: Hanging knee raises
exercises.note: No swinging.

exercises.name: Step-ups
exercises.note: Knee height. Slow, no pushing off the back foot.

exercises.name: Hollow body hold
exercises.note: Lower back stays pressed down.

exercises.name: Single-leg calf raise
exercises.note: Full stretch at the bottom.

exercises.name: Wall handstand + shoulder taps
exercises.note: Add the taps once the hold is solid.

exercises.name: Dips
exercises.note: Heavier day — this is the one to load first.

exercises.name: Chin-ups
exercises.note: Underhand. Easier than pull-ups — that's the point.

exercises.name: Push-ups, feet elevated
exercises.note: 2 seconds down, 1 up.

exercises.name: Pull-up negatives
exercises.note: Jump up, lower over 5 s. This is what builds the pull-up at your level.

exercises.name: Band face pulls
exercises.note: Shoulder health and rear delts. Against this much pressing, it isn't optional.

exercises.name: Seated pike leg lifts
exercises.note: Sit legs straight, hands by your hips, lift the heels off the floor. Compression is what actually gates the L-sit, not core strength.

exercises.name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
exercises.note: Hinge at the hip, back flat, feel the hamstring. Hold the backpack in the opposite hand once bodyweight is easy.

exercises.name: Side plank
exercises.note: Hips stacked and lifted. The only anti-rotation work in the program.

exercises.name: Nordic curl negatives
exercises.note: Lower as slowly as you can, push back up with your hands.

phases.name: Phase 2
phases.span: Starts when you clear the Phase 2 gate.

exercises.name: Wall handstand
exercises.note: Chest to wall. Three long holds, not four short ones. The Phase 3 gate is 60 s, so the range runs to it.

exercises.name: Pull-ups
exercises.note: Normal double progression now. Once you clear 5 on every set, start adding backpack weight.

exercises.name: Dips
exercises.note: Add backpack weight when you clear 12.

exercises.name: Advanced tuck L-sit
exercises.note: Hips open more than a plain tuck.

exercises.name: Hanging straight leg raises
exercises.note: No swinging.

exercises.name: Assisted pistol squat
exercises.note: Box squat, to a lower and lower surface.

exercises.name: Wall handstand negatives
exercises.note: Walk in close, lower slowly to your head, press back up.

exercises.name: Dips
exercises.note: Heavier day — load this one first.

phases.name: Phase 3
phases.span: Starts when you clear the Phase 3 gate. The muscle-up becomes reasonable here.

exercises.name: Free-standing handstand
exercises.note: Kick-up practice against the wall, then away from it.

exercises.name: Explosive pull-ups
exercises.note: Chest to bar. Speed, not grind — stop the set the moment a rep slows down.

exercises.name: Weighted pull-ups
exercises.note: This is where most of the muscle comes from now.

exercises.name: Straight-bar dips
exercises.note: Harder than parallel bars, and the muscle-up needs them.

exercises.name: L-sit, one leg straight
exercises.note: One leg straight, then both.

exercises.name: Band-assisted muscle-ups
exercises.note: Focus on the transition, not the rep. Drop band thickness to progress.
